chunks: "The big one is barrel cracking from thermal cycling.
FR-4 expands a lot along the thickness of the board, roughly 50 to 70 parts per million per degree below its glass transition and several times more above it, and copper only expands about 17.
So every time the board heats, the resin stretches the copper barrel in the Z direction.
After enough cycles, or after a few 260 degree lead-free reflows, the barrel fatigues and cracks, usually at the corner where the barrel meets the pad or in the middle of the barrel.
It shows up as an intermittent open that appears when warm.

Next are manufacturing defects: voids or thin spots in the plating, usually in deep narrow holes with a high aspect ratio, poor desmear so there's resin smear between the inner-layer pad and the barrel, and drill wander that breaks out of the annular ring.
Then there's CAF, conductive anodic filament: in humid conditions with a voltage between two close vias, copper can grow along the glass fibres and create a leakage path or short.
Closer hole spacing makes it worse. At assembly, vias in pads can wick solder and cause voids or opens.
And electrically, too much current through too few vias will overheat or fuse them.
I prevent these with lower aspect ratio, enough plating thickness, adequate via spacing, high-Tg material, more vias in parallel, and filled vias where wicking matters."
